answer: A farm that parks keys in the jury pool thus watches its influence decay while paying the island fee to keep them eligible. Because the quill decay is applied at each close, the reef audit shows the reduced weight and the seat has to be earned again. A juror that skips cases loses 7% of its weight per missed epoch, so sitting on a seat without doing the work is not a passive strategy. A 368 account operation therefore ties up 17 million dollars of idle capital. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
